card.essence: Calcarea carbonica addresses the leucophlegmatic constitution with impaired calcium metabolism, manifesting as deficient bone development, glandular swellings, and profuse sour discharges. The typical patient is fair, fat, flabby, pale, and cold—mentally sluggish yet anxious, physically torpid yet easily fatigued, with characteristic profuse head sweats during sleep that soak the pillow far around.
card.family: Minerals · Calcium Carbonate (middle layer of oyster shell)
card.sides: Right upper lung affinity; right-sided head coldness

keynotes.text: Leucophlegmatic: fair, fat, flabby, pale—tendency to obesity in youth
Head sweats profusely during sleep, wetting pillow far around
Open fontanelles, delayed dentition, soft bones developing slowly
Cold, damp feet—as if wearing cold, damp stockings
Sour: taste, eructations, vomiting, stools, body odour
Craves eggs and indigestible things (chalk, coal, pencils); aversion to meat
Feels better when constipated; stool must be removed mechanically
Takes cold easily, especially in chest; sensitive to cold, damp air
Pit of stomach swollen like inverted saucer

modalities_worse.text: Cold air, wet weather, cold water, washing
Mental or physical exertion, ascending stairs
Pressure of tight clothing around waist

mentals: Apprehensive, worse towards evening; fears loss of reason, misfortune, contagious diseases
Fears people will observe her mental confusion
Forgetful, confused, low-spirited; depressed melancholic mood
Obstinacy; slight mental effort produces hot head
Averse to work or exertion; apathetic, indolent
physicals: Large head and abdomen; fontanelles and sutures remain open
Curvature of spine and long bones; extremities crooked, deformed
Children have no disposition to walk or stand; tardy learning to walk
Swelling of glands: cervical, mesenteric, submaxillary
Profuse perspiration on back of head and neck, or chest and upper body
Girls fleshy, plethoric, growing too rapidly
Menses too early, too profuse, too long; least mental excitement causes profuse return of flow
Gets out of breath easily; short of breath on ascending or exertion
Rawness of soles from perspiration; blisters and offensive foot sweat
Difficult, delayed dentition with head sweats
clinical: Rickets and scrofulous conditions in children with delayed bone development
Incipient phthisis, especially upper third of right lung in tall, slender, rapidly growing youth
Hydrocephalus in infants with profuse head sweats
Dentition troubles with open fontanelles and head sweats
Marasmus and malnutrition from inability to assimilate lime
Chlorosis and anaemia in pale, plump, leucophlegmatic subjects
Diseases arising from working in cold water or standing on cold, damp pavements

differentials.note: Sulphur is lean, stooped, active, nervous, burning, hot; Calcarea is fat, flabby, sluggish, cold. Calcarea follows Sulphur well, especially if pupils dilated.
Lycopodium is bilious, swarthy, yellowish; Calcarea is pale, chalky, white. Both have digestive weakness but different temperaments.
Both have head sweats, open fontanelles, take cold easily. Silica more delicate, yielding, chilly; similar sphere but different constitutional picture. Calcarea acts best before Silica.
Phosphorus more often indicated in lung disease of tall, slender youth, but Calcarea oftener the true constitutional remedy in such cases; Phosphorus burning, desires cold.
Belladonna is the acute of Calcarea; complementary relationship.
Graphites also has obesity but with characteristic skin eruptions (eczema, fissures); Calcarea obesity more primary constitutional feature.

cautions: In aged people should not be repeated; if first dose benefited, repetition will usually do harm
According to Hahnemann, must not be used before Nitric acid and Sulphur—may produce unnecessary complications
In children may be repeated often, but use carefully in elderly
